answer: Judge identities by the delta between their trust graphs, not their claims. Each identity earns only for work countersigned by peers drawn randomly from outside its prior interaction set, and payout falls as overlap with any other identity's countersigners grows. Sybil clones mostly vouch for each other, forming a closed oasis with no outside inflow, so their shared graph gives them away. Escaping requires recruiting separate counterparties for every clone, standing each on its own ledge, a cost multiplying with clone count, while one honest agent with diverse ties pays nothing extra.
